Gabriel Lee and Aya Andersson, we’re sorry for the stress caused by your delayed departure with Benny and the way the update was handled.

You reported that your companion animal travel connection didn’t get the timely communication you expected, and that the delay affected Benny’s scheduled movements between skyports while you were trying to coordinate care and travel plans.

From the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways, we take those concerns seriously. Our role is to guide passengers through companion animal travel, and we also work closely with the crews to keep processes consistent and safe across skyports. When a delayed departure happens, we focus first on safe boarding, animal welfare, and clear, respectful communication. If your experience fell short, that’s on us, and we want to make it right in the ways we can.

<<FACT F109>> 

To prevent a repeat of that situation, the department shares practical instructions with crews and reinforces when updates should be communicated to passengers carrying companion animals. In cases involving a delay, we recommend that travelers keep Benny secure and ready for handling changes, including having a calm transport setup and making sure contact details on file are current so that the crew can reach you quickly if circumstances shift. If you were already doing that, we appreciate it, and we recognize it doesn’t remove the frustration of waiting without enough information.

If you can reply with any specific details you remember about when the update was expected and what you received instead, we can pass that exact feedback to the responsible coordination team. That lets us improve how the senior coordinator and crew support companion animals during disruption, so future travel is smoother for both people and pets.

We understand how important timing is when traveling with a pet, and we’re committed to getting you a reliable resolution and better communication next time.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
